name: Spanish Grand Prix
sources_2026_10_03: Race-story notes added from Formula1.com, FIA, BBC Sport, Mercedes, McLaren, Autosport, ESPN and the Guardian, all 2026-09-13 to 2026-09-14; official FIA final classification used for results and penalties. Data notes: Albon's Q2 slower than his Q1 is verbatim from the FIA classification; Bearman's grid 22 represents a pit-lane start (FIA Doc. 65 lists 21 cars on the grid); Stroll completed 12 laps per FIA Doc. 73 though reports place his stop on laps 13 to 15.
summary: Kimi Antonelli won Madrid's inaugural Spanish Grand Prix by 4.351s from Max Verstappen, with Lando Norris third after an ill-timed VSC and a slow pit stop cost the polesitter a likely win. Lance Stroll's brake failure triggered the VSC, allowing Antonelli, Verstappen and Russell to pit cheaply while Norris and long-running Charles Leclerc stayed out; Leclerc finally stopped late and finished fourth. Four cars retired: Hamilton and Stroll with brake failures, Perez with a suspected water-system issue and Sainz after contact damage, while Gasly's five-second pit-lane penalty and Sainz's five-second race penalty were applied without changing the finishing order.

classification.stewardNote: Race time 1:34:23.754. Won from P2 after gaining track position on Norris when the Virtual Safety Car fell at the ideal moment for his stop. Extends his championship lead over Russell to 81 points.

+4.351s. Cut the opening corner while fighting Hamilton and was instructed by Red Bull to give the positions back, yielding to Antonelli and Hamilton. No time penalty appears in the final classification.
+5.089s. Took pole at 1:31.824 and led early, then lost the race to a badly timed VSC: he stopped under green while Antonelli and Verstappen pitted cheaply under the neutralisation.
